material_units.source_text:
Definition — Lipschitz and locally Lipschitz vector fields
      
        $f$ is Lipschitz on $D$ with constant $L$ if $\|f(x)-f(y)\|\le L\|x-y\|$ for all $x,y\in D$, and locally Lipschitz if every point has a neighbourhood on which it is Lipschitz (equivalently, it is Lipschitz on every compact subset of its domain; for $f$ defined on all of $\mathbb R^n$, on every bounded set). Continuously differentiable functions are locally Lipschitz (Primer B). Example: $x^2$ is Lipschitz with constant $2R$ on $[-R,R]$ but not on $\mathbb R$; $\sqrt{|x|}$ is not Lipschitz on any neighbourhood of $0$; $1/x$ is locally Lipschitz on $(0,\infty)$ but not Lipschitz on the bounded set $(0,1)$, which is not compact.
